recipes.title: Chicken Adobo
recipes.description: Chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay leaves until tender and glossy. The unofficial national dish of the Philippines.
steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce and garlic in a pot and marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Add the water, bay leaves and peppercorns. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil for 2 minutes without stirring to mellow the sharpness.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until slightly thick. Serve with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Sinigang na Baboy
recipes.description: A sour tamarind soup with tender pork belly and vegetables. Comfort food for rainy days.
steps: Boil the pork in water, skimming off the scum, then add the onion and tomatoes.
Simmer for about 1 hour until the pork is tender.
Add the radish and cook for 5 minutes, then the string beans for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind soup base and season with fish sauce.
Add the kangkong, turn off the heat and serve hot.

recipes.title: Mapo Tofu
recipes.description: Silky tofu in a fiery, numbing Sichuan sauce with ground pork and fermented broad bean paste.
steps: Blanch the tofu cubes in salted simmering water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Fry the ground pork until browned, then add the doubanjiang and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the stock, slide in the tofu and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry, pushing the tofu gently so it doesn't break.
Finish with Sichuan pepper and scallions. Serve over rice.

recipes.title: Egg Fried Rice
recipes.description: Fluffy day-old rice tossed in a hot wok with egg, scallions and soy sauce. Ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Pour in the eggs and scramble until just set, then break them into small pieces.
Add the rice and toss constantly for 3 to 4 minutes until every grain is hot.
Season with soy sauce and white pepper, then fold in the scallions and serve.

recipes.title: Kimchi Fried Rice
recipes.description: Tangy, spicy fried rice made with well-fermented kimchi and topped with a runny fried egg.
steps: Stir-fry the kimchi in a little oil for 3 minutes until slightly caramelized.
Add the rice, kimchi juice and gochujang and fry until evenly red and hot.
Drizzle with sesame oil and divide between two bowls.
Fry the eggs sunny side up, place one on each bowl and top with seaweed.

recipes.title: Bibimbap
recipes.description: A colorful rice bowl with seasoned vegetables, beef, a fried egg and spicy gochujang sauce, mixed together just before eating.
steps: Marinate the beef in soy sauce, sugar, garlic and sesame oil for 15 minutes.
Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately and season each with sesame oil and salt.
Sauté the carrot and mushrooms separately, then cook the beef over high heat.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Arrange everything over the rice, top with an egg and serve with gochujang to mix in.

recipes.title: Chicken Teriyaki
recipes.description: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs glazed in a sweet and savory homemade teriyaki sauce.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar into a sauce.
Place the chicken skin side down in a cold pan, then cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp.
Flip and cook for another 5 minutes. Wipe out the excess fat.
Pour in the sauce and simmer, spooning it over the chicken until glossy and thick.
Slice and serve with rice, drizzling the remaining glaze on top.

recipes.title: Miso Soup
recipes.description: A light, savory soup of dashi and miso with tofu, wakame and scallions. Ready in 10 minutes.
steps: Soak the wakame in water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi until just below a simmer.
Dissolve the miso in a ladle of the warm dashi, then stir it back into the pot. Don't let it boil.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm through for 1 minute.
Serve topped with scallions.

recipes.title: Adobong Dilaw
recipes.variantNote: Fresh turmeric instead of soy sauce turns it golden.
recipes.description: Batangas adobo, golden with fresh turmeric and sharp with cane vinegar. Earthy, tangy and lighter than the soy version.
steps: Combine the pork, turmeric, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns and salt in a pot and leave for 30 minutes.
Add the water and bring to a boil. Let it boil for 2 minutes without stirring to mellow the vinegar.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Uncover and cook until the sauce reduces and the pork starts to fry in its own fat.
Taste for salt and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Adobo sa Gata
recipes.variantNote: Finished with coconut milk and chilies.
recipes.description: Adobo the Bicolano way: the vinegar braise is finished in coconut milk with chilies, so it comes out creamy, tangy and hot.
steps: Put the pork, vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns in a pot and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the pork is tender.
Uncover and reduce until most of the liquid is gone.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the chilies and simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes until thick and the oil starts to separate.
Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Adobong Puti
recipes.variantNote: No soy sauce: just vinegar, garlic and salt.
recipes.description: White adobo, made without soy sauce. Vinegar, garlic and salt let the pork taste of itself, and it finishes crisp in its own fat.
steps: Put the pork, vinegar, half the garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, salt and water in a pot.
Bring to a boil without stirring, then cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Uncover and let the liquid cook off until the pork renders its fat.
Add the rest of the garlic and fry everything until the edges of the pork turn golden.
Serve with rice and a dipping vinegar.

recipes.title: Sinigang na Hipon
recipes.description: A lighter sinigang with head-on shrimp in tamarind broth. Quick enough for a weeknight.
steps: Boil the water with the tomatoes and onion for 5 minutes.
Add the radish and cook for 5 minutes, then the okra and string beans for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind soup base and season with fish sauce.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink.
Add the kangkong, turn off the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Sinigang na Bangus
recipes.description: Sour tamarind soup with milkfish, eggplant and mustard greens. Clean-tasting and comforting.
steps: Boil the water with the tomatoes and onion for 5 minutes.
Add the eggplant and chilies and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind soup base and season with fish sauce.
Slide in the milkfish and simmer gently for 8 minutes without stirring, so it stays whole.
Add the mustard greens, cook for 1 minute and serve.

recipes.title: Sinigang sa Miso
recipes.description: Sinigang with miso stirred into the broth, which makes it rounder and more savory. Best with oily fish.
steps: Sauté the onion and tomatoes until soft, then add the miso and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil and add the radish.
Stir in the tamarind soup base, add the fish and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the chilies and mustard greens and season with fish sauce.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Sinigang sa Bayabas
recipes.description: Sinigang soured with ripe guava instead of tamarind. Sweeter, fragrant and traditionally made with milkfish.
steps: Boil the guavas in the water for 15 minutes until very soft.
Mash the guavas, strain them through a sieve and return the liquid to the pot.
Add the tomatoes and onion and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the milkfish and string beans and simmer for 8 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, add the kangkong and serve.

recipes.title: Pancit Malabon
recipes.variantNote: Thick rice noodles under an orange shrimp sauce, piled with seafood.
recipes.description: Thick rice noodles coated in a shrimp and annatto sauce, then loaded with seafood, smoked fish, eggs and crushed chicharon.
steps: Pound the shrimp heads with 2 cups of water and strain to make a shrimp broth.
Simmer the broth with the annatto powder and fish sauce until slightly thickened.
Soak and boil the noodles until tender, then drain.
Cook the shrimp and squid separately in a little oil.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, top with the seafood, smoked fish, chicharon, eggs and scallions, and serve with calamansi.

recipes.title: Pancit Habhab
recipes.variantNote: Miki noodles eaten straight off a banana leaf, with a splash of vinegar.
recipes.description: Lucban street noodles served on a square of banana leaf and eaten without utensils, with vinegar poured on top.
steps: Sauté the garlic, onion and pork for 5 minutes, then add the liver and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and broth and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and cook, stirring, until they absorb the liquid.
Add the chayote, carrot and bok choy for the last 2 minutes.
Serve each portion on a banana leaf with vinegar on top, and eat it straight off the leaf.

recipes.title: Pancit Batil Patong
recipes.variantNote: Noodles topped with ground beef and an egg, with egg-drop soup on the side.
recipes.description: Tuguegarao noodles crowned with ground beef, vegetables and an egg on top (patong), served with a beaten-egg soup (batil).
steps: Brown the ground beef and liver with half the onion and season with soy sauce.
Stir-fry the noodles with a splash of broth and soy sauce, then add the bean sprouts and cabbage.
Fry one egg per serving and place it on top of the noodles and beef.
Bring the rest of the broth to a boil and stir in the remaining beaten eggs to make an egg-drop soup.
Serve the noodles with the soup on the side, chopped onion and scallions.

recipes.title: Sapporo Miso Ramen
recipes.variantNote: Rich miso broth topped with sweet corn and a pat of butter.
recipes.description: The ramen of Hokkaido: a hearty miso broth with stir-fried pork and bean sprouts, finished with corn and melting butter.
steps: Stir-fry the garlic, ginger and pork in sesame oil until browned, then add the bean sprouts for 1 minute.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer, then whisk in the miso off the boil.
Cook the noodles according to the package and drain well.
Put the noodles in bowls and ladle the soup over them.
Top with the pork and sprouts, corn, a pat of butter and scallions.

recipes.title: Hakata Tonkotsu Ramen
recipes.variantNote: Milky pork-bone broth with thin, firm noodles.
recipes.description: Fukuoka ramen: pork bones boiled hard for hours into a creamy white broth, with thin straight noodles cooked firm.
steps: Blanch the bones for 10 minutes, then drain and scrub them clean.
Cover with fresh water, add the garlic and ginger, and boil hard for 10 to 12 hours, topping up with water. The hard boil turns the broth milky.
Strain the broth and put the soy sauce and salt into each bowl.
Boil the noodles for about 1 minute so they stay firm.
Pour the broth over the seasoning, add the noodles and top with chashu, scallions, red ginger and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Tokyo Shoyu Ramen
recipes.variantNote: Clear chicken and dashi broth seasoned with soy sauce.
recipes.description: The classic Tokyo bowl: a clear amber broth of chicken and dashi, soy sauce seasoning and wavy noodles.
steps: Simmer the chicken gently in water for 2 hours, skimming often so the broth stays clear.
Steep the kombu and then the bonito flakes in the hot stock for 10 minutes, then strain.
Warm the soy sauce and mirin together and put 2 tablespoons in each bowl.
Cook the noodles and add them to the bowls with the broth.
Top with chashu, menma, nori and scallions.

recipes.title: Kitakata Ramen
recipes.variantNote: Soy broth of pork and dried sardines over thick, wavy, chewy noodles.
recipes.description: From Fukushima: a soy-seasoned broth of pork bones and dried sardines, thick curly noodles and a lid of sliced pork.
steps: Simmer the pork bones gently for 3 hours for a clear stock.
Soak the dried sardines and kombu in water for 1 hour, simmer for 10 minutes, strain and combine with the pork stock.
Put 2 tablespoons of soy sauce in each bowl.
Cook the thick noodles for about 4 minutes and add them to the bowls with the broth.
Cover the noodles with chashu slices and top with menma and scallions.

recipes.title: Jeonju Bibimbap
recipes.variantNote: Rice cooked in beef bone broth, topped with many namul and beef tartare.
recipes.description: The famous bibimbap of Jeonju: rice cooked in beef broth, a ring of seasoned vegetables and seasoned raw beef in the center.

ingredients.name: very fresh beef sirloin, finely julienned

steps: Cook the rice in the beef bone broth instead of water.
Blanch or sauté each vegetable separately and season each with sesame oil, garlic and salt.
Season the raw beef with soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil just before serving.
Arrange the vegetables in a ring over the rice, with the beef and an egg yolk in the center.
Serve with gochujang and mix everything together at the table.

recipes.title: Jinju Bibimbap
recipes.variantNote: Topped with seasoned raw beef, with a clear bean-sprout soup on the side.
recipes.description: Bibimbap from Jinju, topped with seasoned raw beef and served with a light soybean-sprout soup.
steps: Cook the rice.
Simmer half the soybean sprouts in salted water with a little garlic for 10 minutes to make the side soup.
Blanch the remaining sprouts and the spinach, sauté the bracken, and season each with sesame oil and salt.
Season the beef with soy sauce, sesame oil and garlic.
Top the rice with the vegetables, beef and crumbled seaweed, and serve with gochujang and the soup.

recipes.title: Dolsot Bibimbap
recipes.description: Bibimbap served in a sizzling stone bowl, so the rice at the bottom turns into a crisp golden crust.
steps: Prepare and season the vegetables and beef.
Heat the stone bowls on the stove and brush the insides with sesame oil.
Pack the rice into the bowls, arrange the toppings and crack an egg on top.
Heat over medium for 5 to 7 minutes until the rice crackles and a crust forms.
Add gochujang and mix at the table, scraping up the crispy rice.

recipes.title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
recipes.variantNote: A white fried rice: no dark soy, seasoned with salt and stock.
recipes.description: Fried rice from Yangzhou with shrimp, ham, peas and egg. Pale and clean-tasting, because it uses salt and stock instead of dark soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Chinese ham or char siu, diced

steps: Scramble the eggs softly in a hot wok and set aside.
Stir-fry the shrimp and ham for 1 to 2 minutes and set aside.
Fry the peas and carrot, then add the rice and toss until every grain is hot and separate.
Season with salt and chicken stock, with no soy sauce.
Return the eggs, shrimp and ham, fold in the scallions and serve.

recipes.title: Hokkien Fried Rice
recipes.variantNote: Egg fried rice under a thick, savory seafood gravy.
recipes.description: Fujian-style fried rice: simple egg fried rice with a glossy gravy of seafood, chicken and mushrooms poured over the top.
steps: Make a simple egg fried rice: scramble the eggs, add the rice, season lightly and plate it.
Stir-fry the chicken, then the mushrooms, shrimp and scallops.
Add the stock, oyster sauce and soy sauce, then the bok choy, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Thicken with the cornstarch slurry until glossy.
Pour the gravy over the rice and serve.

ratings.comment: Lots of prep but worth it.
